title: εἰ conditions
subtitle: Separate the condition from its conclusion.
overview: An εἰ clause states the supposition (the if-part); the other clause gives its consequence.
Do not infer that a condition is true or false merely from εἰ. Read the verbal forms and context.

sections.title: Condition and conclusion
rows: If you believe, you will be saved
If you do this, you do well
εἰ ἦν ἐνθάδε, οὐκ ἂν ἀπέθανεν
If he had been here, he would not have died

items.grc: εἰ ὁ θεὸς μεθ᾽ ἡμῶν, τίς καθ᾽ ἡμῶν;
items.en: If God is for us, who is against us?

items.grc: εἰ ἀγαπᾶτέ με, τὰς ἐντολὰς τηρήσετε.
items.en: If you love me, you will keep the commandments.
